newsitem.title: UK: Diana, shocked by nudes, drops Versace book entry.
newsitem.headline: Diana, shocked by nudes, drops Versace book entry.

text.p: Princess Diana withdrew her support for a fund-raising book by Italian designer Gianni Versace on Friday, fearing the British royal family might take offence at being pictured alongside near-naked men.
Versace -- one of Diana's favourite designers -- responded by cancelling a planned London book launch "to protect" the princess and by donating money to an AIDS charity.
The furore began when Diana agreed to back a coffee-table book on music and royals aimed at helping AIDS victims.
"I was assured that the book would not contain material which would cause offence and I therefore signed the foreword," Diana told Britain's Press Association news agency.
"Earlier this week I saw a copy for the first time.
"I am extremely concerned that the book may cause offence to members of the royal family. For this reason I have asked for my foreword to be withdrawn," the Princess of Wales said.
Rock and Royalty, already on sale in Italy, Germany and the United States, is believed to contain pictures of semi-naked models and celebrities opposite pictures of the royal family.
A photograph of the late Duke and Duchess of Windsor, for example, sits opposite Manchester United footballer Ryan Giggs, who is wearing a crown and appears to have his genitals exposed.
Versace said the book was created to benefit the rock star Elton John's AIDS charity, "not to cause a scandal".
"There are actually no nudes in this book. The pictures used are all beautiful images from some of the best photographers of our century," he said in a statement.
